input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: a Content-Type parameter without an equals sign is stored with the value True instead of being skipped
- failure path: the header `text/html; charset` yields params['charset'] == True; get_encoding_from_headers (shown below the change) returns params['charset'].strip(...) which raises AttributeError on a bool, so reading response.text for such a response fails instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1

Reviewer finding
- description: A Content-Type parameter without '=' (e.g. 'text/html; charset') is now stored as the boolean True, so the 'charset' lookup returns True and calling .strip() on it raises AttributeError.
- rationale: Trigger: a response header 'Content-Type: text/html; charset' with no value. The new code in _parse_content_type_header sets params['charset'] = True instead of skipping the token. get_encoding_from_headers then reaches params['charset'].strip(...), which fails on a bool. Before this change the token was ignored and the function fell through to the 'text' branch and returned ISO-8859-1. The impact is an exception while reading a malformed but previously tolerated response, so the caller crashes instead of getting a fallback encoding.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. A valueless parameter is stored as True instead of being skipped, then `.strip()` is called on the bool in get_encoding_from_headers and raises AttributeError. The previous behavior fell back to ISO-8859-1.
